root_cause.text: In ep_remove(), the file’s f_ep pointer is cleared without preventing a concurrent __fput() from seeing the transient NULL and freeing the file while ep_remove() still accesses it, causing a use-after-free on both the struct file and the watched struct eventpoll.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that “ep_remove() cleared file->f_ep under file->f_lock but then kept using @file inside the critical section … A concurrent __fput() taking the eventpoll_release() fastpath in that window observed the transient NULL, skipped eventpoll_release_file() and ran to f_op->release / file_free().” The patch fixes this by pinning @file via epi_fget() at the top of ep_remove().

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a race condition in ep_remove by safely obtaining a reference to the file to prevent use after free when eventpoll_release_file is concurrently executing.
intent_record.what: Changed ep_remove to use epi_fget() with __free(fput) instead of directly accessing epi->ffd.file, restructured the dying check by removing the spin_lock/unlock around epi->dying check and moving it before the lock, and updated the comment.
intent_record.how: The function now obtains a reference to the file via epi_fget(), which returns NULL if the epitem is dying, avoiding race with eventpoll_release_file(). The file pointer is automatically fput'd on function exit via __free attribute. The spin_lock is only taken after successfully acquiring the reference.

grouping_result.intent: Fix a race condition in ep_remove by safely obtaining a reference to the file to prevent use after free when eventpoll_release_file is concurrently executing.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent and changes directly address the race condition in ep_remove that leads to use-after-free, which is the core vulnerability described.

candidates.rationale: Obtains a pointer to the file without incrementing its reference count, so a concurrent __fput() can free the file while ep_remove() still uses it.
Directly accesses the file's spinlock without ensuring the file is still alive; if the file has been freed, this causes a use-after-free.
Passes the potentially freed file pointer to ep_remove_file, which will use it, leading to use-after-free on both the file and the watched eventpoll.
Accesses epi after the file may have been freed; ep_remove_epi may use the file or eventpoll structures that are no longer valid.

Accesses epi after the file may have been freed; ep_remove_epi may use the file or eventpoll structures that are no longer valid due to the race condition.
